messages.subject: softmax
parts:
Hi,

I am not sure if it is by design or not.

I am receiving a message
Invalid value of theta: validate transformed params(d): theta is not a valid simplex. sum(theta) = -1.#IND:0, but should be 1

while in my code I have
    positive_ordered [K] theta_raw;
and
    simplex [K] theta;
 
    theta <- softmax (theta_raw);

I am still using 2.6.0 rstan.

Thank you,
Linas

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] softmax
parts:
For instance, this runs OK, but if you remove the prior,
then it won't work because the posterior will be improper.


parameters {
positive_ordered[5] theta_raw;
}
transformed parameters {
simplex[5] theta;
theta <- softmax(theta_raw);
}
model {
theta_raw ~ normal(0,2);
}


- Bob

messages.author: cab04b8f0759c712
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] softmax
parts: If you used the simplex as a parameter and didn't use softmax to transform, there would be a uniform prior over simplexes and you wouldn't have a problem. The issue is that you're taking a positive_ordered parameter and using a softmax to create a simplex. The posterior over a positive_ordered parameter, without anything else in the model, is improper.

On Mon, May 4, 2015 at 7:15 PM, Linas Mockus <linasm...@gmail.com> wrote:
Thanks, Bob.  This is the case.  Since theta is simplex I assumed it will be uniform.  Should I use normal instead?

Thank you,
Linas
